opening_message:
Ticket 1: Dominic Taylor (employee ID E004) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E004.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Dominic Taylor (E004) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code, owned by the Engineer role. Full-time employees may have up to write, and the role owns the system, so write is within policy.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E004 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Since training is basic, maximum is read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes for E004 conflict on employment type: HR states full-time Engineer (which would permit write to Source Code), while Security states contractor with basic security training (which caps access at read). Given the unresolved contradiction and the conservative principle of least privilege, I grant the maximum level supported by the more restrictive set of facts: read. Write requires advanced training for contractors, which E004 does not have.
